clinical.rationale: Head-to-head comparison of six bedside scores supports selecting AIR score for ED risk stratification of complicated appendicitis.

research.rationale: Multicenter prospective comparison with AUC, calibration, and decision curve analysis offers a transferable evaluative framework.

papers.one_line: In 360 children with appendicitis, the AIR score best identified complicated disease (AUC 0.78), outperforming five other scoring systems.

summary.why_it_matters: Early identification of complicated appendicitis may guide surgical timing and resource use; comparing practical scores helps clinicians choose an effective tool.

summary.bottom_line: The AIR score appears superior for ED risk stratification of complicated appendicitis in school-aged children, although external validation in broader populations is needed.

papers.methods_note: Multicenter prospective study with head-to-head AUC comparison, calibration analysis, and decision curve analysis.

summary.why_it_matters: Neonatal sepsis is a leading cause of death in sub-Saharan Africa, and current management is uniform. A simple, admission-based risk stratification tool could help target care and resources.
summary.design: Retrospective multicentre cohort study using latent class analysis on signs of possible serious bacterial infection at admission, with external validation in separate hospitals.
